src/nexara_prime/brain/evolution_engine..summary: EvolutionEngine — unified evolution loop with human approval boundary. Collects candidates from 4 sources (reflection/experience/preference/mission_intelligence), evaluates proposals, gates through risk-based autonomous boundary, and drives a full lifecycle: DRAFT → EVALUATING → APPROVAL_REQUIRED/APPROVED → APPLIED → VERIFIED → ARCHIVED.

tests/brain/phase2d/test_evolution_engin.summary: Comprehensive test suite with MockMC simulating MemoryController. Covers proposal creation, candidate collection from all 4 sources, evaluation (high/medium/low risk), approval boundary, apply/reject/verify/archive flow, history retrieval, summarization, full lifecycle, and edge cases.

tests/brain/phase2d/test_isolation.py.summary: Isolation tests verifying no forbidden imports (runtime, model_gateway, tools, evidence, governance, cli, api, db) in evolution_engine.py, confirming MemoryController usage, and regression-checking prior phase files exist.

design_quality.separation_of_concerns: EXCELLENT — EvolutionController depends only on MemoryController via constructor injection. No runtime, model gateway, tool, evidence, governance, CLI, API, or direct DB imports. Clean boundary.
design_quality.state_machine: GOOD — 7 statuses with VALID_TRANSITIONS DAG. evaluate_proposal() gates correctly: risk > 0.7 or confidence < 0.3 → DRAFT; risk > 0.4 → APPROVAL_REQUIRED; else APPROVED. apply guards on APPROVED, verify guards on APPLIED.
design_quality.single_responsibility: STRONG — EvolutionController does one thing: manage the evolution proposal lifecycle. Delegates storage to MemoryController.
design_quality.testability: EXCELLENT — MockMC in tests mirrors real MemoryController interface. Fixtures, seed helpers, and test classes organized by concern. All 4 source types tested independently plus empty case.
design_quality.extensibility: GOOD — SOURCE_TYPES and TARGET_AREAS are lists; adding new sources is straightforward. _from_* methods follow a consistent pattern.

positive: TYPE_CHECKING guard on MemoryController import — clean, no circular deps
Risk/confidence clamping in evaluate_proposal (0.1–0.9) prevents degenerate values
Proposal IDs are content-addressed (SHA-256 of source+target+change+timestamp) — deterministic and unique
Full lifecycle test exercises all states end-to-end
Edge cases tested: verify non-applied (no-op), archive non-verified (accepted — documented), confidence clamping at boundaries
Summarize() returns structured counts by status, source_type, and target_area
reject_proposal increments risk_score by 0.1 (capped at 1.0) — prevents infinite rejection loops
verify_evolution increments confidence by 0.1 (capped at 1.0) — positive reinforcement on verification
archive_evolution has no status guard — allows archiving from any state (flexible, documented in tests)
No forbidden imports confirmed by isolation tests — clean architecture enforcement
observations: VALID_TRANSITIONS is defined but never enforced at runtime — transitions are validated implicitly by status guards in apply/verify methods, but a transition validation helper could catch invalid state changes
_make_proposal imports hashlib inside the method — minor; could be module-level for clarity
MockMC.commit() uses positional arg fallback with kw.get() — works but is fragile if MemoryController signature changes
get_evolution_history() filters by key prefix 'evolution:' and status='active' — archived proposals with status='active' would still appear, which may be intentional
archive_evolution does not guard on status (unlike apply/verify which require APPROVED/APPLIED) — intentional design choice per test comment, but worth documenting in the method docstring
_record_proposal always sets status='active' on commit — status field on the stored record is separate from proposal.status; may cause confusion between record status and proposal status
risks: NONE CRITICAL — No runtime coupling, clean dependency graph, comprehensive tests

review.verdict: APPROVED — Phase 2D Evolution Engine is well-architected, properly isolated from runtime/dependencies, comprehensively tested (21+ test methods), and follows a clean state machine lifecycle with a clear human approval boundary at risk_score > 0.4.
